full_text_zh:
[P1] 七夕的故事
连环画出版社

[P2] 七夕的故事
司南/改编
马得/绘画

很久很久以前，有个小伙子，每天都上山放牛。大家看到他和那头老牛形影不离，就叫他牛郎。

连环画出版社

[P3] 牛郎的爹妈早没了，哥哥嫂嫂对他不好，整天
让他吃剩饭剩菜，干苦活累活。即使这样，哥嫂还要跟他分家。
老牛悄悄对牛郎说：“分家就分家，你什么都别
要，就要我这头老牛吧！”

[P4] 牛郎答应了，带着老牛离开了家。
有一天，王母娘娘的女儿们偷偷飞到人间，想要痛快地玩一玩。

[P5] 王母娘娘的第七个女儿叫织女。她听到美妙的乐曲，走近一看，原来是牛郎在吹牧笛。
织女对牛郎说：“我喜欢人间的生活，想跟你在一起，好吗？”牛郎也喜欢织女，毫不犹豫地答应了。

[P6] 他们请老牛做“媒人”，欢欢喜喜地结了婚。
牛郎种田，织女织布，日子过得很美满。
几年后，他们生了一儿一女。孩子长得很健康，又活泼又可爱。

[P7] 谁知好景不长，王母娘娘派来的天兵找到了织女，要把她捉回天宫去。

牛郎伤心地说不出话来，孩子们哭叫着：“妈妈、妈妈，你别走！”

[P8] 但是没办法，织女只能跟着天兵飞回天宫。

牛郎挑起箩筐，担着两个孩子去追织女！
老牛说：“他们在天上飞，你在地下跑，怎么追得上呢？”他摘下头上的角，交给牛郎。

[P9] 牛郎挑着孩子，把牛角往空中一扔。牛角立刻
变大了，像一只弯弯的小船。牛郎踏上小船，忽地
飞了起来。

追呀，追呀，牛郎终于追上了织女。孩子们一
下子扑上来抱住了妈妈。

[P10] 狠心的王母娘娘看见了，她冷笑一声，拔下头
上的簪子，向空中一划……

牛郎和织女之间立刻出现了一条大河！

[P11] 织女和孩子们都哭了，牛郎愤怒地说：“就是一
勺一勺地舀，我也要把河水舀干！

这时，数不清的喜鹊飞了过来，在河上搭起了
一座鹊桥。一家四口在桥上团聚了！

[P12] 你看，银河两侧闪闪发光的就是牛郎星和织女星。牛郎星两侧还有两颗小星星，那就是他们的孩子。

七夕是女孩子们的节日，所以，又叫“乞巧节”。最早的时候，盛行让姑娘们同时拿着一根针、一根线比赛穿孔，看谁穿得快，谁把线先穿进针孔，就算是“乞”到“巧”了。后来，到了明清，特别流行在“七夕”的上午，玩一种“丢巧针”的游戏。先端一碗水在太阳底下晒着，等一会儿，水面就会产生一层薄膜，然后将平时缝衣服或者绣花用的针投到水碗里面，针就浮在水面上了。丢针的人再去看水底的影子，如果有花朵、鸟兽、云彩的影子，或者细直如针一样，那个人就是巧的。这些影子表示织女赐给她一根灵巧的绣花针，可以织绣出美丽的图案。如果水底针影粗如槌，或者弯曲不成形，这就表示丢针的女孩子是个“拙妇”，因为织女给她的是 一根石杵。

除了用针，有些女孩子也会用蛛网乞巧。办法是把蜘蛛放在盒中，看它结的网的样子，结得

[P13] 密，就说明“乞”到“巧”了。
“乞巧”之余，女孩子们也常常会拜银河。拜银河，也叫拜双星。女孩子们几个一伙约好，推选家里有花园的当主办者，供案设在葡萄架旁边，上面摆着蜜桃、闻香果等时令水果，花瓶里插上鲜花。祭拜以后，女孩子们围坐在一起边吃边聊天。也有一些小姑娘会头上顶着红布，蹲到葡萄架下面，去听牛郎、织女相会时的哭声。
除了女孩子，小孩子们也都喜欢这个节日。宋代的时候，到了“七夕”可以买到很多好玩的东西，有一种玩具叫做“磨喝乐”，也就是用泥巴做成的玩偶，小泥偶手里拿着荷叶，十分可爱；此外还有蜡制的小鱼、小鸭、小鹅和鸳鸯等，称为“水上浮”；各色各样的油炸小点心称为“巧果”；商贩在瓜果上雕刻出花样，将未开放的莲花两枝扎成并蒂。孩子们在集市上流连忘返，迟迟不肯回家去。
full_text_en:
[P1] The Story of Qixi
Lianhuanhua Publishing House

[P2] The Story of Qixi
Adapted by Si Nan
Illustrated by Ma De

Long, long ago, there was a young man who went up the mountain to herd cattle every day. Everyone saw him and the old ox always together, so they called him Niulang.

Lianhuanhua Publishing House

[P3] Niu Lang's parents had passed away long ago. His brother and sister-in-law treated him poorly, making him eat leftovers and do hard, tiring work all day. Even so, his brother and sister-in-law still wanted to divide the family property with him.
The old ox whispered to Niu Lang, "If you're going to divide the family, don't take anything else—just take me, this old ox!"

[P4] Niulang agreed and left home with the old ox.
One day, the daughters of the Queen Mother secretly flew to the mortal world, wanting to have a good time.

[P5] The seventh daughter of the Queen Mother of the West is called Zhinü. She heard a beautiful melody and, upon approaching, saw that it was Niulang playing his shepherd's flute.
Zhinü said to Niulang, "I like life on earth. Would you like to be together with me?" Niulang also liked Zhinü and agreed without hesitation.

[P6] They asked the old ox to be their 'matchmaker' and happily got married.
Niulang farmed the fields, and Zhi Nu wove cloth; their life was very happy and fulfilling.
A few years later, they had a son and a daughter. The children were healthy, lively, and adorable.

[P7] Alas, the happy days did not last long. The heavenly soldiers sent by the Queen Mother found Zhinü and were about to take her back to the heavenly palace.

Niulang was heartbroken and could not speak. The children cried out, “Mom, mom, don’t go!”

[P8] But there was nothing to be done; Zhinü could only follow the heavenly soldiers back to the celestial palace.

Niulang picked up the baskets and carried his two children to chase after Zhinü!
The old ox said, "They fly in the sky, while you run on the ground—how can you catch up?" He took off his horn and handed it to Niulang.

[P9] Niulang carried his children and threw the cow's horn into the air. The horn instantly
enlarged, becoming a small, curved boat. Niulang stepped onto the boat and suddenly
flew up.

Chase, chase! Niulang finally caught up with Zhinü. The children
immediately rushed forward and hugged their mother.

[P10] The cruel Queen Mother saw this, she sneered and pulled out the hairpin from her head, drawing it through the air...

Immediately, a great river appeared between Niulang and Zhinü!

[P11] Zhi Nu and the children cried. Niulang angrily said, “Even if I have to scoop it out spoon by spoon, I will drain the river dry!

At this moment, countless magpies flew over and built a bridge across the river. The family of four reunited on the bridge!

[P12] Look, the shining stars on both sides of the Milky Way are Altair and Vega. On both sides of Altair, there are two small stars — those are their children.

The 7th Day of the 7th Lunar Month is a festival for girls, so it's also called the "Qiqiao Festival". In ancient times, girls would compete to thread a needle with a piece of thread, and whoever did it fastest was considered to have "begged" for skill. Later, during the Ming and Qing dynasties, it became popular to play a game called "dropping the clever needle" on the morning of the 7th Day. One would place a bowl of water in the sun, wait for a thin film to form on the surface, then drop a needle used for sewing or embroidery into the water. The needle would float. The person who dropped the needle would then look at its shadow at the bottom of the bowl. If the shadow resembled flowers, birds, animals, or clouds, or was straight like a needle, that person was considered skillful. These shadows were said to mean that the Weaver Girl had granted her a clever needle for embroidery, allowing her to create beautiful patterns. If the shadow was thick like a mallet or bent and misshapen, it meant the girl was clumsy, as the Weaver Girl had given her a stone pestle.

Besides using needles, some girls also used spider webs to beg for skill. The method was to put a spider in a box and observe the shape of the web it spun, and if the web was well-formed, it was considered a good omen.

[P13] Dense, it means 'qǐ' has reached 'qiǎo'.
After 'qǐ qiǎo', girls often worship the Milky Way. Worshiping the Milky Way is also called worshiping the Double Stars. Girls gather in groups, choose a host from a household with a garden, set up an altar beside the grapevine, place seasonal fruits like honey peaches and fragrant fruits on it, and put fresh flowers in vases. After the worship, the girls sit together, eating and chatting. Some young girls even put red cloth on their heads and crouch under the grapevine to listen to the crying sounds of Niulang and Zhinü meeting.
Besides girls, children also love this festival. In the Song Dynasty, on the 'Qixi' Festival, many fun things could be bought. There was a toy called 'Móhēlè', made of clay, with a small clay figure holding a lotus leaf, very cute; there were also wax-made small fish, ducks, geese, and mandarin ducks, called 'water floats'; various fried snacks were called 'qiǎo guǒ'; vendors carved patterns on melons and fruits, and tied two unopened lotus flowers together as 'twin blossoms'. Children lingered in the market, reluctant to go home.
full_summary_zh:
[P1] 本页为绘本《七夕的故事》的封面，画面中牛郎挑着两个孩子在水中行走，织女在水边回首凝望，背景为波浪和装饰性边框。
[P2] 本页为绘本《七夕的故事》的扉页和第2页，介绍了故事的开端：很久以前，有个小伙子每天上山放牛，因与老牛形影不离，被大家称为牛郎。
[P3] 本页讲述了牛郎自幼失去父母，被哥哥嫂嫂虐待，被迫分家；老牛劝他不要要其他财产，只带走自己。
[P4] 本页分为左右两页，左页描绘牛郎骑着老牛离开家，右页描绘王母娘娘的女儿们飞到人间游玩。
[P5] 织女被牛郎吹奏的牧笛声吸引，走近后两人相识并互生好感，织女主动提出想与牛郎在一起，牛郎欣然答应。
[P6] 牛郎和织女在老牛的帮助下结为夫妻，过上美满生活，并生下了一儿一女。
[P7] 王母娘娘派天兵捉走织女，牛郎伤心无言，孩子们哭喊着不让妈妈离开。
[P8] 织女被天兵强行带回天宫，牛郎挑着两个孩子追赶，老牛为助他追赶，摘下自己的角交给牛郎。
[P9] 牛郎用老牛的角变出小船，带着孩子飞向天宫，终于追上织女，孩子们扑向妈妈。
[P10] 王母娘娘拔下头上的簪子划向空中，牛郎和织女之间立刻出现了一条大河，将他们隔开。
[P11] 牛郎决心用勺子舀干银河，与织女和孩子们团聚；喜鹊们飞来搭成鹊桥，一家四口在桥上重逢。
[P12] 本页左侧描绘了牛郎星、织女星及其两个孩子在银河两侧的景象，并配有文字解释；右侧介绍了七夕节的传统习俗，如“丢巧针”和“蛛网乞巧”，并配以插图。
[P13] 本页介绍了七夕节的传统习俗，包括女孩们拜银河、听牛郎织女相会的传说，以及宋代孩子们在集市上购买磨喝乐、水上浮、巧果等节日玩具和点心的场景。
